label: Allows children's spouses
summary: Whether the knight rules allow the spouses of the ruler's children to serve as knights.
details: The Knights window binds it to a checkbox state. ToggleAllowSpousesOfChildren is the matching click handler.

label: Allows wounded
summary: Whether the knight rules allow characters with the wounded trait to serve as knights.
details: The Knights window binds it to a checkbox. The matching toggle is ToggleAllowWithTraitWounded.

label: House filter choice
summary: The number of the entry currently chosen in the knight rules' house filter list.
details: The Knights window uses it as the selected entry of a selection list; the choices come from KnightsView.GetHouseFilterOptions and SetHouseFilterIndex stores a new choice.

label: Minimum prowess
summary: The minimum prowess (martial skill) the knight rules ask for, as a whole number.
details: The Knights window shows it as text, and a button there is enabled only when the value is not zero. Vanilla changes it with AdjustMinProwess on the same rules.

label: Vassal filter choice
summary: The number of the entry currently chosen in the knight rules' vassal filter list.
details: The Knights window uses it as the selected entry of a selection list; the choices come from KnightsView.GetVassalFilterOptions and SetVassalFilterIndex stores a new choice.

label: Rules are default
summary: Whether the knight rules are still the default ones.
details: Vanilla uses it with Not: a part of the Knights window is shown, and the knight tooltip adds an extra line, only when the rules were changed from the default.

label: Reset knight rules
summary: Sets all knight rules back to their default values.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Itself
summary: The knight rules object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Set house filter
summary: Stores the entry the player picked in the knight rules' house filter list.
details: Vanilla runs it from the selection-changed event of the list in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Set vassal filter
summary: Stores the entry the player picked in the knight rules' vassal filter list.
details: Vanilla runs it from the selection-changed event of the list in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow concubines
summary: Switches whether concubines may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow councillors
summary: Switches whether councillors may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow inspired
summary: Switches whether inspired courtiers may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow lovers
summary: Going by its name, switches whether lovers may serve as knights, on or off. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it, so this rests on the name and on the sibling toggles, which are click actions in the Knights window.

label: Toggle allow non-combat posts
summary: Switches whether holders of non-combat court positions may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle other children
summary: Switches the 'Other Children' box of the knight permissions on or off.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from that box in the knights window, under family relations; GetAllowOtherChildren reads its state. Exactly which children count as 'other' is not said in the files.

label: Toggle allow player heir
summary: Switches whether the player's heir may serve as a knight, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow pregnant
summary: Switches whether pregnant characters may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow spouses
summary: Switches whether spouses may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle allow children's spouses
summary: Switches whether the spouses of the ruler's children may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. GetAllowSpousesOfChildren reads the current state.

label: Toggle allow wounded
summary: Switches whether characters with the wounded trait may serve as knights, on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in the Knights window. GetAllowWithTraitWounded reads the current state.

label: This knights view
summary: Going by its name, gives the Knights window's data object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type, so this is a guess from the name.

label: Can be acclaimed knight
summary: Whether the given character can be made an acclaimed knight (a knight with an accolade).
details: Vanilla passes the character as `Character.Self` and uses the result with Not, to show a block in the accolade creation window and in a tooltip when the answer is no. Going by its name, KnightsView.CanBeAcclaimedKnightDesc is the matching reason text.

label: Acclaimed knight reason
summary: Going by its name, the text that says whether or why the given character can become an acclaimed knight.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a tooltip block, passing the character as `Character.Self`. It is probably the explanation for CanBeAcclaimedKnight; the input does not say more.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Close Knights window
summary: Closes the Knights window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click handlers of close buttons in the Knights window. It returns nothing.

label: Create random accolade
summary: Going by its name, creates a random accolade. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it, so what it picks and for whom is not shown.

label: Destroy accolade
summary: Going by its name, destroys an accolade. The game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument. The only related line in vanilla is an `Accolade.DestroyAccolade` click in the accolade window, which may be a different type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the accolade to destroy; the input does not say.

label: Accolade slot tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for an accolade slot.
details: Vanilla uses it in the Knights window, in a choice that picks between this text and another one depending on whether the slot's index is below the number of free accolade slots. The meaning of the argument is not shown in the input.

label: House filter options
summary: The list of choices for the knight rules' house filter.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a selection list in the Knights window. GetHouseFilterIndex and SetHouseFilterIndex on the knight rules read and store which one is chosen.

label: Knight rules
summary: The knight rules (who may serve as a knight) that the Knights window works on.
details: It leads on to the KnightPermissions functions, such as IsDefault or AdjustMinProwess. Vanilla uses it in the Knights window and in the knight tooltip text.

label: Military view
summary: The military view object that the Knights window uses as its data context.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of the Knights window. Other lines of that window read `MilitaryView.GetCharacter` and the accolade slots.

label: Locked accolade slots
summary: Going by its name, the number of accolade slots that are locked for the given character. The game documents nothing more.
details: It takes one argument and returns a whole number. Vanilla's files never use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Probably the character; the input does not say.

label: Possible accolade types
summary: The list of accolade types that the given character could get.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a list in a tooltip, passing the character as `Character.Self`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character to list accolade types for.

label: Vassal filter options
summary: The list of choices for the knight rules' vassal filter.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of a selection list in the Knights window. GetVassalFilterIndex and SetVassalFilterIndex on the knight rules read and store which one is chosen.

label: Has candidate knights
summary: Going by its name, whether a stored list of possible acclaimed knights is available.
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the character has a free accolade slot to decide whether to show a part of the Knights window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has possible accolade
summary: Whether the given character could get an accolade.
details: Vanilla uses it in the accolade creation window, together with checks that the accolades feature is active and that the character has no land titles or only a barony as primary title.

label: Shows inactive accolades
summary: Going by its name, whether the Knights window currently shows inactive accolades. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it. ToggleInactiveAccolades looks like its switch.

label: Itself
summary: The Knights window's data object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Toggle inactive accolades
summary: Going by its name, switches the display of inactive accolades on or off. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it. It returns nothing.

label: This succession
summary: Going by its name, gives the Kurultai succession object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Opposing electors
summary: The number of Kurultai electors counted as opposing, as a whole number.
details: The My Realm text shows it in front of the word "Opposes". Its counterpart is GetObedientCount. What exactly they oppose is not stated in the input.

label: Kurultai electors
summary: The list of electors who vote in the Kurultai succession.
details: The My Realm window shows the electors from it, and hides that part when the succession is invalid or the list is empty.

label: Approving electors
summary: The number of Kurultai electors counted as approving, as a whole number.
details: The My Realm text shows it in front of the word "Approves", and a progress bar uses it as its value (converted to a decimal number). Its counterpart is GetDisobedientCount. What exactly they approve is not stated in the input.

label: Succession status text
summary: The tooltip text describing the state of the Kurultai succession.
details: The My Realm window shows it as a text.

label: Vote count
summary: The number of votes in the Kurultai succession, as a whole number.
details: The My Realm window shows parts only when it is above 0, and uses it as the maximum of a progress bar; one use also asks whether the player is a nomad.

label: Is stable
summary: Whether the Kurultai succession is stable.
details: The My Realm window shows one part when it is stable and another when it is not. What 'stable' requires is not stated in the input.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether the Kurultai succession is valid. The game documents nothing more.
details: The My Realm window shows its Kurultai parts only when it is true. One other line shows something when a bookmark succession is set and this is not true. What makes it valid is not stated in the input.

label: Itself
summary: The Kurultai succession object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This title template
summary: Going by its name, gives the title template object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms of the title template.
details: It leads on to coat of arms functions. Vanilla chains it as BookmarkCharacter.GetLandedTitleTemplate.GetCoA.GetTexture(...) in the bookmark screens.

label: Itself
summary: The title template object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This map icon
summary: Going by its name, gives the landless rulers map icon object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Domiciles
summary: The list of domiciles (homes of landless rulers) that belong to this map icon.
details: The map icon layer uses it as the data of a list, skipping the first entries up to and including the first valid domicile, which the icon shows separately.

label: First valid domicile
summary: The first valid domicile of this map icon.
details: The map icon layer uses it as the data context of the main part of the icon.

label: First valid domicile index
summary: The position of the first valid domicile in the icon's list of domiciles, as a whole number.
details: The map icon layer adds 1 to it and skips that many entries of the domicile list, so the list of further domiciles starts after the first valid one.

label: Province
summary: The province the map icon sits in.
details: The map icon layer uses it as the data context of the icon. Going by its name and use, it is the province the icon is drawn on.

label: Valid domicile count
summary: The number of valid domiciles at this map icon, as a whole number.
details: The map icon layer shows parts only when it is above 0 or above 1. A text shows it minus 1, as a '+' number for the further domiciles.

label: Itself
summary: The landless rulers map icon object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Should show ruler
summary: Whether the given ruler should be shown on this map icon.
details: The map icon layer uses it as a visibility condition, passing the character as `Character.Self`.

label: This language window
summary: Going by its name, gives the language window object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Close language window
summary: Closes the language window.
details: Vanilla runs it from close buttons in the language window. It returns nothing.

label: Grandest royal court
summary: Going by its name, the grandest royal court, as an object the language window can take a character from.
details: Vanilla only uses it followed by GetCharacter, as the data context of a part of the window. What "grandest" compares is not stated in the input.

label: Language
summary: The language that the language window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window's content. The input does not say what kind of object it is.

label: Ranked royal courts
summary: A ranked list of royal courts for the language window.
details: Vanilla shows that part of the window only when the list has items, and uses it as the data of the list.

label: Opened from royal court
summary: Whether the language window was opened from a royal court.
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the Royal Court DLC feature is on: one part of the window is shown when both are true, another when either is not.

label: Itself
summary: The language window object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This law
summary: Going by its name, gives the law object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Confirm button text
summary: The text of the confirm button when adding this law.
details: A localization key uses it directly as its text.

label: Confirm window title
summary: The title of the confirmation window when adding this law.
details: A localization key uses it directly as its text.

label: Effect description
summary: The text that describes what the law does.
details: Vanilla shows it in the law choice tooltip, in the succession law change window and in the window for adding a law to a title.

label: Enact breakdown
summary: The tooltip text that breaks down what enacting the law means for the player.
details: The window for adding a law to a title shows it as a tooltip. The input does not show what the breakdown lists.

label: Enact cost
summary: The text of the cost the player pays to enact the law.
details: The window for adding a law to a title shows it as a text.

label: Enact effect description
summary: Going by its name, the text that describes what enacting the law does for the player. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it. GetTitleEnactEffectDescriptionForPlayer is the version that takes a title and is used.

label: Icon
summary: The icon image of the law.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image in the ledger, the migration window and the My Realm window. HasIcon tells whether the law has one.

label: Index
summary: Going by its name, a whole number that identifies the law's position. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files do not use it on a law. The game uses the same name on other types, for example in legitimacy texts, which is only a hint. GetIndexInLawGroup is the one vanilla uses for a law.

label: Index in law group
summary: The law's position within its law group, as a whole number starting at 0.
details: Vanilla adds 1 to show it as the law's level in My Realm texts, and checks that it is 0 or more in the migration window.

label: Key
summary: Going by its name, the law's internal key as text. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `GetKey` on other types, which is a hint. LawGroup.GetKey is used there to compare against names like 'camp_purpose'.

label: Law group
summary: The law group this law belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it to check a flag on the group ('realm_no_pass') in a pass-law text, and as the data context in a tooltip.

label: Name
summary: The law's display name, with a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in many texts, such as 'X can not be applied to titles'. GetNameNoTooltip gives the same name without the tooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The law's display name as plain text, without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in titles and button texts such as 'Pass X Law'.

label: Pass law phrase
summary: The phrase used to pass this law.
details: Vanilla uses it in a tooltip title: if the law is already enacted the law's name is shown, otherwise this phrase.

label: Short name
summary: The short name of a law, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the message that a ruler changed a law of a law group 'from … to …', for both the old and the new law.

label: Short name without tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the law's short display name as plain text. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `GetShortNameNoTooltip` on activities, which is a hint.

label: Subtitle
summary: The law's second line of name, shown as a subtitle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the law tooltip's subtitle and in the succession change and add-law windows. HasSubName tells whether there is one.

label: Enact effect for title
summary: The text that describes what enacting the law does on the given title.
details: The window for adding a law to a title shows it, passing the window's title.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The title the law would be enacted on.

label: Has flag
summary: Going by its name, whether the law has a given flag. The game documents nothing more.
details: The game's documentation lists two arguments, but vanilla's similar uses (such as `Law.GetLawGroup.HasFlag( 'realm_no_pass' )`) give one text. The input does not show what the second one is, so this stays uncertain.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; vanilla's similar calls pass the flag name here.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the law has an icon.
details: A tooltip uses it as a visibility condition for the icon part. GetIcon gives the icon.

label: Has subtitle
summary: Whether the law has a subtitle.
details: The succession change and add-law windows show the subtitle line only when it is true. GetSubName gives the subtitle.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether the law object exists. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `IsValid` on other types, such as a government, which is a hint.

label: Localize
summary: Going by its name, turns the given text key into text in the current language. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `Localize( ... )` as a general function on other types, which is a hint.

label: Itself
summary: The law object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This law group
summary: Going by its name, gives the law group object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Can ruler change
summary: Whether the given ruler can change the laws of this law group.
details: The My Realm window uses it as the enabled condition of a part of the window, passing the player.

label: Index
summary: Going by its name, a whole number that identifies the law group's position. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `GetIndex` on a legitimacy type, which is a hint.

label: Key
summary: The law group's internal key as text.
details: Vanilla compares it with fixed names such as 'camp_purpose' and 'nomadic_authority' in a tooltip to hide a part for those groups.

label: Name
summary: The law group's display name.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as 'Change the X law from A to B'.

label: Singular name
summary: Going by its name, the law group's display name in singular form. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's only related line is `GuiLawGroup.GetLawGroup.GetNameSingular` in My Realm, shown as a label ending in a colon, which fits this reading.

label: Has flag
summary: Whether the law group has the given flag.
details: Vanilla checks flags such as 'treasury_budget_law' (in My Realm) and 'realm_no_pass' (in a pass-law text).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a flag name in quotes, such as 'treasury_budget_law'

label: Is cumulative
summary: Going by its name, whether the laws of the group add up instead of replacing each other. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether the law group object exists. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `IsValid` on other types, such as a government, which is a hint.

label: Localize
summary: Going by its name, turns the given text key into text in the current language. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla only shows `Localize( ... )` as a general function on other types, which is a hint.

label: Itself
summary: The law group object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This law item
summary: Going by its name, gives the law list item itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Law
summary: The law that this list item stands for.
details: The window for adding a law to a title uses it as the data context of each entry.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this law item is the selected one in the list.
details: The window for adding a law to a title uses it for the 'pressed' look and for showing a part only when the item is not selected.

label: Select law item
summary: The action run when the law item is clicked, presumably selecting it.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button finishes its action in the add-law window. It returns nothing.

label: Itself
summary: The law list item itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This layer
summary: Going by its name, gives the layer object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Itself
summary: The layer object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This tree item
summary: Going by its name, gives the layer tree item itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Entry
summary: The map object entry behind a row of the map editor's layer tree.
details: Vanilla shows the entry's key (GetKey) in the rows for meshes, entities, locators and generated objects. The game gives a generic return type.

label: Instance count
summary: How many copies of a map object a row of the map editor's layer tree stands for, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in yellow next to the layer name and next to each mesh, entity and locator entry. That it counts the placed copies is read from the name.

label: Layer name
summary: The name of the layer a row of the map editor's layer tree stands for, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in bold as the row's label, next to its fold mark and instance count.

label: Is expanded
summary: Whether a row of the map editor's layer tree is opened to show its entries.
details: Vanilla shows a '+' mark while it is no and a dash while it is yes.

label: Is generated
summary: Going by its name, whether the tree item was generated automatically. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it.

label: Is hidden
summary: Whether a layer of the map editor's layer tree and its map objects are hidden.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the row's hide button, whose tooltip reads 'Hide this layer and map objects'.

label: Is layer
summary: Whether a row of the map editor's layer tree is a layer, not one of its entries.
details: Vanilla shows the hide button for layer rows and an empty spacer in its place for the other rows.

summary: Whether the map objects of a row of the map editor's layer tree are locked.

details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the row's lock button (tooltip 'Lock these map objects').

label: This icon

details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Icon layer
summary: One layer of a layered icon, as a picture.

fields.name: argument 1

summary: The layered icon itself, so it can be handed on as a value.

label: This contract type
summary: Going by its name, gives the lease contract type itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the lease contract type.
details: A shared tooltip shows it as a text.

summary: Going by its name, the lease contract type's internal key as text. The game documents nothing more.

label: Name
summary: The name of a lease contract type, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in a holding's tooltip, after the holder, as the title's lease contract (reached through the title's GetLeaseContractType).

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The lease contract type's display name as plain text, without a tooltip.
details: A shared tooltip shows it as a text.

label: Itself
summary: The lease contract type itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This window
summary: Going by its name, gives the lease-out-baronies window object itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Can confirm
summary: Going by its name, whether the lease-out-baronies window can be confirmed. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla uses `CanConfirm` on other windows to enable the confirm button, which is only a hint.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the lease-out-baronies window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a close button of the window. It returns nothing.

label: Selection hint
summary: Going by its name, a hint text about what to select in the window. The game documents nothing more.
details: Vanilla's files never use it.

label: Titles
summary: The list of titles (baronies) the window offers to lease out.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data of the list, and shows an extra part when the list is empty.

label: Confirm
summary: Confirms the lease-out-baronies window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the click of the window's confirm button. It returns nothing.

label: Itself
summary: The lease-out-baronies window object itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This title item
summary: Going by its name, gives the title list item itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Title
summary: The title (barony) that this list item stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the item and to show the title's name.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether this title is selected in the lease-out list.
details: Vanilla uses it for the 'pressed' look of the item and to show a mark only when it is selected.

label: Select title
summary: The action run when the title item is clicked, presumably selecting or unselecting it.
details: Vanilla runs it from the item's click handler. It returns nothing.

label: Itself
summary: The title list item itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This ledger item
summary: Going by its name, gives the ledger artifact item itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact that this ledger row stands for.
details: The ledger window uses it as the data context of the row and shows its name without a tooltip.

label: Itself
summary: The ledger artifact item itself, so it can be handed on as a value.
details: Going by its name and by how game texts use `Self` (as an argument, such as `Character.Self`), it returns the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: This ledger item
summary: Going by its name, gives the ledger character item itself, for passing on. The game documents nothing more.
details: Game files only show the same function name as `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` passed as an argument, which may be a different type.
